newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds stable as punt steadies after sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds stable as punt steadies after sell-off.

text.p: Irish bonds stabilised in early trade on Thursday as the punt steadied after plummeting the previous day when it came under selling pressure amid concerns that its high exchange rate in the ERM was unsustainable, dealers said.

Dealers said the punt's fall of more that four pfennigs on Wednesday was probably enough to stem more selling in the short term, but in the long term it faced the same problem - a market belief that it will enter a single currency at its central ERM rate of 2.41 marks, more than 14 pfennigs below its current level.
"The market is all over the place," one dealer said.

"We have seen some form of stability after the big sell-off in the currency and bond markets yesterday. But the Irish market seems unsure about where it is going for the moment. A lot of people are staying on the sidelines," the dealer added.
By 0820 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 10 pence at 102.10 to yield 5.94 percent. The key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was also up 10 pence at 109.10 to yield 6.65 percent.
The Irish pound was trading at 2.5648/98 marks compared with 2.5566 in late trade on Wednesday. It was at 0.9200/30 stg versus 0.9180, and $1.5108/23 versus $1.5110.
